h1: Window cleaning in Hughes Park Lake
intro: Hughes Park Lake is a small lakefront subdivision off Hughes Park Road on a cove of Lake Travis in 78732. CleanzATX washes the windows on waterfront estates here.

sections.h2: What Hughes Park Lake homes are like
paragraphs: The subdivision is small and sits right on a cove. Lots here have sold from around $330,000, and the waterfront estates reach as high as $6.5 million, so the homes range widely from modest lots to large houses. There is no gate. Hughes Park Road is the way in.
A waterfront house is built around its view. Expect decks, balconies and tall glass on the lake side, often over more than one level.

sections.h2: What Hughes Park Lake windows deal with
paragraphs: On the water, mist and humidity do much of the damage. Lake water carries minerals, and when droplets dry on glass they leave spots that can etch. Sprinklers and the occasional high water day add to it. Cedar and live oak pollen settle on top in winter and spring.
Glass on balconies and decks sits low to the water and picks up spots faster than upper floor windows. West facing panes show every streak in afternoon sun, so a spot free finish matters.

sections.h2: How we work Hughes Park Lake
paragraphs: Estates here often have glass on two or three levels, and our poles reach up to three stories from the ground, so we can work from the yard or driveway. With a waterfront lot, we ask about the best place to park and which side faces the sun. Windows pair naturally with pressure washing on decks and flatwork, using a surface cleaner for flat areas and hand cleaning near the house.
Because homes vary so much, we quote by text after seeing photos. A 4,500 square foot waterfront home would be around $450 for exterior glass, and the visit would take about four hours.

why: Glass over two or three levels is reachable from the ground with our poles.
Waterfront mist and sprinkler spots both come off with pure water.
Large range of home sizes, so we quote each one from photos.
Deck and flatwork washing can be done during the same visit.

faq.q: Do you clean glass on lakefront decks and balconies?
faq.a: Yes. We clean what the poles reach from the ground and wash decks by hand near the house. For tall balconies, text a photo and Tyler will tell you exactly what he can reach.

faq.q: How are estates priced, given how different they are?
faq.a: By window count or square footage. Exterior glass is $10 per window, or about $0.10 per square foot. Minimum job is $200. A photo helps us give a closer number.

faq.q: Does lake water leave spots that are hard to remove?
faq.a: It can. Minerals harden over time and may etch. We remove them for $10 per pane and keep new ones off with regular pure water cleaning.

faq.q: Can you also wash my dock area?
faq.a: We wash patios and pool decks by hand and flatwork with a surface cleaner. Ask in your text about a dock and Tyler will say whether it is something we handle.

faq.q: How soon can you schedule a visit?
faq.a: Usually within two weeks. Quotes by text come back within the hour during business hours, and we confirm the day the week before.
